text:
Justin Hryckowian's first NHL stretch was a nice undrafted story: 86 games, 14 goals, a Northeastern product who earned his way to Dallas. Year two has been harder. He has two goals and three points in 22 games and one point in his last 10, and he's playing about 15 minutes a night to get them.

Some of that is finishing (two goals on 2.9 expected), but less of it than you'd hope. His chance rate has dropped from 0.73 expected goals per 60 last season to 0.52, and the Stars are 5 points worse in expected-goal share with him on the ice than without him. His team isn't getting unlucky around him either; the on-ice results are close to what the chances deserve.

Evolving-Hockey had him worth 1.0 wins above replacement last season, mostly from even-strength offense, so there is a better version of this player on record. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking notes he carries the puck in on only 30% of his entries, so his line lives off dump-ins and the forecheck. With Dallas winning most nights, the minutes may not last if the chances don't come back. Our range still has him around 26 points.
